Program Supervisor, Fire Prevention and Preparedness

Are you passionate about fire prevention and preparedness and looking for an opportunity to work with an organization that is dedicated to improving the lives of residents from diverse backgrounds? Do you want to use your leadership experiences to influence community growth?

If this sounds like your ideal career, then Toronto Community Housing is the place for you!

We are searching for a collaborative and strategic team player who enjoys working in a dynamic and energetic environment. In this role, you will get to work with a team of internal and external partners support TCHC in fire prevention and preparedness activities in a manner that supports TCHC’s tenant focused culture.

What You’ll Do

Provide day-to-day leadership, direction and support to a team of Fire Prevention Inspectors, ensuring inspections, reporting and follow-up activities are completed consistently and in accordance with legislative requirements;
Coordinate and oversee the Fire Prevention Inspection Program, including inspection scheduling, workload planning, quality assurance and program performance;
Monitor inspection findings, identify trends and emerging risks, and use data to develop risk-based inspection strategies that prioritize higher-risk buildings and support continuous program improvement.
Review inspection reports, Fire Code contraventions and recommendations, providing technical guidance and support to Fire Prevention Inspectors on complex or unique compliance matters.
Liaise with TFS, consultants, contractors and internal stakeholders to resolve fire and life safety issues, obtain approvals and support ongoing compliance;
Coordinate the development, review and maintenance of Fire Safety Plans to ensure site-specific accuracy and compliance with legislative and code requirements;
Inspect, read and interpret building plans, blueprints, installation guides, construction plans and specifications as well as notice of violations and inspection orders;
Prepare procurement documents, oversee service contracts and monitor vendor performance to ensure quality service delivery;
Lead public education and fire prevention initiatives by coordinating awareness campaigns, reviewing educational materials and supporting consistent messaging for staff and tenants;
Prepare reports and maintain records detailing information about property, infractions observed and actions to be taken;
Establish client communication protocols, financial reporting mechanisms, progress updates, scheduling and work activities to meet/exceed contract obligations;
Supervise, mentor, train and direct unionized service and administrative staff;
Manage staff’s attendance including vacation requests, payroll input and monitoring of staffing capacity (shifts, on call, call-out schedules, etc.);
Track false fire alarm incidents and work with TFS Public Education on methods to reduce the number of occurrences as well as the reducing the financial impact on TCHC.
Other projects/initiatives and duties as required.

What You’ll Need

Post-Secondary education in Fire Protection Technology, or an equivalent of combination of directly relevant education and experience;
Minimum of 3-5 years of job-related experience including technical and legislative knowledge and experience in contract administration, tender preparation, and development and monitoring of budget plans;
Demonstrated knowledge of the Ontario Fire Code, Ontario Building Code, Occupational Health and Safety Act, Residential Tenancies Act and other related legislation, by-laws and applicable standards;
Excellent interpersonal/ public relations/teamwork skills;
Experience in the preparation of reports, correspondence and record maintenance;
Possesses strong negotiating skills and the ability to analyze and evaluate complex problems provide solutions and recommend alternatives;
Possesses advanced skills in computer applications such use of Microsoft Word, Project and Excel;
Excellent communication skills both oral and written;
Excellent customer service skills and experience in providing respectful service;
Previous experience in dealing with the public in enforcement situations or experience in construction, architecture or engineering is an asset.
Experience supervising unionized staff would be considered an asset;

What's Next

Once you apply, we’ll review your resume to determine if your skills and experience match the qualifications for the role and only qualified candidates will be contacted for next steps. If you move forward, the process may include an interview, written/practical test, and reference check.

INDS

Thank you for your interest in Toronto Community Housing

We recognize that people bring experience and talent that goes beyond the technical skills and requirements of a job. If you possess similar experience that is close to what we’ve included in the job postings below, we encourage you to consider applying. We strongly believe that diverse experience, transferable skills, and passion are key!

Once you have submitted your application successfully, you will receive a confirmation email. We encourage you to check out our careers page often, as new opportunities become available on a regular basis.

Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion

We are committed to providing equal opportunity to all employees and strive to create a diverse workplace that reflects the cultural mosaic of our great city and the communities we serve. We recognize the value that comes from different viewpoints, unique experiences and diverse perspectives of our employees, who bring fresh, new ideas to our business. The Social Worker monitors the patient’s progress throughout hospitalization and documents relevant findings with regard to Social Services and discharge planning in a timely manner. Prioritizes and Facilitates discharge planning in a timely manner for those with post-acute care needs in order to avoid unnecessary delays
Maintains documentation in medical record and Midas.
Interviews patients/significant others within one working day of referral to obtain data on personal, social, medical, emotional, cultural, and religious history in order to delineate problems requiring Social Work intervention and to plan appropriate services.
Collaborates with the multidisciplinary team members regarding discharge planning and arranges for needed care in the home or an alternate setting.
Consults, assesses, refers, coordinates interventions in cases of suspected or actual situations of child or abuse and neglect or other forms of domestic violence and/or sexual abuse.

Facilitates patient/family and provider meetings as necessary to develop and plan strategies related to psychosocial and economic issues, particularly those related to care progression and transition. May act as the liaison between patients/families and all providers of care within and external to the organization on social issues.
Works collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to identify patients at risk for rehospitalization, and mediates barriers to successful discharge plan.
Works collaboratively with the Multidisciplinary team in assisting individual patients and their families to maximize function and independence by researching, accessing, or referring appropriate services and community agencies.
Assists the multidisciplinary team to assess psychological and social aspects of patient care needs, and collaborates on plan of care interventions.
Prepares and maintains individual patient and departmental records according to department, federal and state regulations; completes statistical information and prepares correspondence as needed.

Strong leadership ability and excellent interpersonal skills, as well as, solid oral and written communication skills.

jobs.description:
Description

Are you an experienced Program Manager who thrives on bringing structure, momentum and clarity to complex transformation? This is an opportunity to play a central role in an enterprise program, helping to coordinate and deliver the people activity initiatives that will support a major technology-enabled transformation across the organisation.

Working closely with the HR Program Lead, HR Talent Lead, HR Leadership Team, workstream delivery teams and HRIT, you will ensure activities are well planned, coordinated, tracked and delivered against clear objectives and timelines. You will be the connective tissue across multiple delivery teams, bringing disciplined execution, strong stakeholder management and the ability to navigate ambiguity in a fast-moving global environment.

This is an 18-month fixed-term contract and can be a fully remote role, giving you the flexibility to work from anywhere in the UK, with optional office access if desired. As an alternative location, we will also consider candidates based in the US Eastern Time Zone.

The Role

Partner with workstream delivery teams and project managers to turn transformation objectives into practical delivery plans, milestones and execution roadmaps.
Build and maintain integrated program plans, milestone trackers, RAID logs, risk registers and status dashboards to provide clear visibility of progress.
Drive day-to-day program execution, ensuring activities remain aligned to agreed objectives, timelines and outcomes.
Identify and manage dependencies, constraints, risks and critical path activities, escalating issues with clear recommendations and mitigation options.
Coordinate across delivery teams to ensure key deliverables are completed on schedule and to agreed quality standards.
Provide structured updates to program leadership and stakeholders on progress, risks, issues, dependencies and decisions.
Establish and manage governance cadences, including steering committee reviews, workstream check-ins and escalation protocols.
Build strong working relationships with HRLT, HRIT, Internal Comms and Change Management, Legal, Finance, AI TMO and functional leaders.
Ensure HRIT and change management deliverables are integrated into program planning, readiness, training and communications activity.
Promote best practice program management standards and capture lessons learned to improve future transformation initiatives.
Ensure the program is aligned to and tracking against the financial goals and targets (investment, savings).

Qualifications

What you’ll bring

Significant project or program management experience delivering complex global transformation in a large enterprise environment.
Experience in HR transformation, operating model transformation, technology-enabled change or large-scale business change programs.
A track record of managing multiple cross-functional projects or workstreams simultaneously, including dependencies, risks and stakeholder expectations.
Experience supporting executive governance forums and preparing clear, decision-focused leadership reporting materials.
Strong stakeholder management, facilitation and meeting management skills, with the confidence to drive alignment and decisions in ambiguous environments.
Structured and disciplined delivery skills, with the ability to translate strategic objectives into practical plans and measurable outcomes.
Working knowledge of both waterfall and agile or hybrid delivery methodologies.
An analytical mindset, with confidence using data, metrics and technology to inform decisions and status reporting.

Start making the most of your career and wellbeing with a range of benefits tailored for you.

The Global Real Estate and Facilities (GREF) organization seeks a strategic support partner to transform how we leverage AI-powered insights and translate them into critical execution plans across our EMEA portfolio. jobs.title: Master Social Worker - MSW
jobs.description:
PURPOSE AND SCOPE:

Provides psychosocial services to patients treated by the facility including in-center and home dialysis patients (if applicable) utilizing Social Work Theory of Human Behavior and accepted methods of social work practice. Works with the health care team to promote positive adjustment, rehabilitation and improved quality of life for our patients. In collaboration with the interdisciplinary team, informs, educates and supports staff in understanding the emotional, psychological and behavioral impact of Chronic Kidney Disease on the patient and family to ensure comprehensive quality care of our patients. Supports the Fresenius Kidney Care (FKC) commitment to the Quality Indicators and Outcomes and Quality Assessment and Improvement (QAI) Activities, including those related to patient satisfaction and quality of life and actively participates in process improvement activities that enhance the likelihood that patients will achieve the FKC Quality Goals. This is an entry level MSW role.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Patient Assessment / Care Planning / Counseling
As a member of the interdisciplinary team, assesses patients' psychosocial status, strengths and areas of need that may affect rehabilitation and optimal treatment outcomes as part of the comprehensive patient assessment.
Participates in care planning in collaboration with the patient and healthcare team to identify effective interventions that will help the patient meet rehabilitation, treatment goals, and improve quality of life.
Utilizes FKC patient education programs, established social work theory and methods, social work focused interventions, and quality of life measurement instruments as part of assessment and care planning to address barriers and meet patient treatment goals.
Provides monitoring and interventions for the patient to adjust to dialysis and achieve optimal psychosocial status and quality of life.
Provides supportive counseling services to patients as permitted within the scope of their clinical training and state license.
Provides educational and goal directed counseling to patients who are seeking transplant.
Provides information and assists the team and patient with referral to community resources (home health services, vocational rehabilitation, etc.) to facilitate optimal treatment outcomes.
Maintains current knowledge regarding local vocational/educational rehabilitation programs and assist patients with referral and access to vocational rehabilitation to enable them to remain employed, become employed or receive education.
Assesses patient awareness of advance directives; assists with accessing advance directive forms/information and facilitates discussion of advance directive wishes, if necessary, with the healthcare team and the patient's family/support persons.
In collaboration with the physician and nurse, participates in the discussion of patient DNR status in the facility to ensure patient and/or family understand and make an informed decision about their care.
Knowledgeable of and adheres to FMCNA Social Work Policy and Measuring Patient Physical and Mental Function Policy, including documentation.
Documents based on MSW interaction and interventions provided to patient and/or family.

Quality
Provides psychosocial support and/or Social Work Focused Interventions to address non-adherence, quality outcome, and quality of life concerns for all patients based on acuity level.
Participates in monthly Quality review meetings with the interdisciplinary team. Reports on quality indicators related to adherence, such as Missed and Shortened Treatments, Quality of Life Trends, and Service Recovery.

Patient Education
Assesses patient knowledge of kidney disease for barriers that may affect adherence to treatment. Works with patient, family and health care team to provide education tailored to the patient’s learning style, communication barriers, and needs.
With other members of the interdisciplinary team, provides appropriate information about all treatment modalities.
Facilitates the transplant referral process and collaborates with interdisciplinary team on transplant waitlist management.
Provides ongoing education to patient/family regarding psychosocial issues related to End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) and all support services that are available.
Reviews patient rights and responsibilities, grievance information (company and network) and other facilities policies with patient and/or the patients’ representative to ensure patients’ understanding of the rights and expectations of them.
Collaborates with the team on appropriate QAI activities.

Patient Admission and Continuity of Care
Reviews Patient Rights and Responsibilities, Grievance Procedure & Important Numbers Handout, FKC Non-discrimination policy, DNR Statement (if applicable) and address any immediate needs/concerns.
Understands the referral and admission process and supports the clinic in regard to the patient needs for scheduling to maximize adherence and adjustment.
The Social Worker will interview the patient to identify root causes or concerns for the discharge request, (i.e. transfer to hospice, relocation, dissatisfaction with services or staff) and share causes/concerns with operational leadership.

Insurance and Financial Assistance
Collaborates and functions as a liaison for patient with Insurance Coordinators to address issues related to insurance.
In collaboration with Insurance Coordinators, provides information and education to patients about payment to dialysis (federal, state, commercial insurance, state renal programs, AKF HIPP, and entitlement programs).
Collaborates with the Insurance Coordinator of any changes to patient state that impacts insurance i.e. transplantation, discharged, loss of coverage, or extended travel.
Refers patients to patient billing solutions (PBS) department for questions/concerns in regard to treatment related bills

Staff Related
Assists with interview process and decision to hire new personnel if requested by SW Manager/Senior Manager.
Works with the administrative support staff to maintain updated patient resource lists (e.g. maintain updated list of transportation resources).
Provides training to staff pertaining to psychosocial topics as needed.
Contributes and participates with weekly team huddles. Discusses any urgent patient issues with staff.

Adheres to work defined caseload guidelines based on state regulatory requirements.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

new_jobs.title: Senior Case Manager - Remote
new_jobs.description:
Church World Service, Inc. (“CWS”) is a not-for-profit, faith-based organization transforming communities around the globe through just and sustainable solutions to hunger, poverty, displacement, and disaster.

About CWS

Imagine waking up every morning with the chance to change someone's life. Imagine knowing your efforts will benefit both your career and our neighbors around the world. At CWS, our team knows they are making a difference every day. Whether you're in our U.S.-based offices supporting refugees, asylees or unaccompanied children ... implementing hygiene initiatives in Cambodia or rebuilding projects in Central America ... or even connecting remotely from your home on fundraising campaigns, grant reports, or critical communications - you have the opportunity to work towards a world where everyone has food, a voice and a safe place to call home.

Purpose

The Senior Case Manager provides culturally humble and client-centered services to support 100 % virtual case management for newcomers across diverse geographies in the U.S. The role accompanies newly arrived immigrants or recently granted asylees facing barriers to access the tools, information and services they need to thrive in their communities. The position conducts outreach, virtual screening, assessment, case management, resource creation and service coordination referrals through unique, individual case management plans, in line with program guidelines.

This role also supports the timely administration of rental assistance in line with funder requirements. In many cases, the role may coordinate with other ORR service providers, immigration legal service providers and other community-based organizations to coordinate continuum of care and help program participants meet their needs and achieve self-sufficiency goals. Additionally, the position will conduct research and outreach to a wide array of community service providers to advocate for access for clients to promote local integration in a diverse number of locations.

This is a grant funded position through the Preferred Communities Supplemental funding and is expected to last through September 2027.

Responsibilities

Handle complex and difficult, or crisis case situations.
Conduct comprehensive assessments for clients with varying needs
Develop support plans and coordinate services required with in-house programs and various outside agencies
Document all contacts and services in client case files and maintain case note logs. In addition to documenting all services, record clients’ public assistance usage. Complete all required reports.
Advocate for clients to ensure the client applies for all federal, state, local or non-governmental programs for which the client qualifies. Provide support and crisis intervention when needed.
Keep informed about client immigrant issues, changing federal policies and available services to clients, using current information to better identify and serve clients.
Establish and maintain strong relationships with community agencies, social services and professional providers.
Continuously monitor complex progress and evaluate effectiveness of support plans and recommend changes as needed.
Perform all duties in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.
Undertake other duties as assigned.
Must be 21 years of age.

Position Specific Responsibilities & Skills

Welcome and orient clients to the community through the provision of program
Secure appropriate and affordable housing for new clients; develop relationships with local landlords.
Empower clients to formulate realistic yet ambitious employability plans.

Its end-to-end Command, Control, Computers, Communications and Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance (C4ISR) capabilities encompass design, integration, test, certification, ground/flight training and complete logistics support. Track and report on project status, technical execution, and overall program performance.

Current Active Secret Security Clearance

Understanding with application tools and data architectures.

Experience with ensuring compliance with approved Corporate and ISO 9001:2000 Policies and Processes.

Essential Functions

Ability to work in an office or hybrid environment.
Frequent use of a computer and standard office equipment.
Must be able to communicate effectively with team members and stakeholders.
Occasional travel may be required to support project needs and team collaboration.

new_jobs.title: Engineering Program Manager, NA Field Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Description

Application deadline: Aug 29, 2026

Amazon is seeking an Engineering Program Manager to support the Amazon Logistics North America (AMZL NA) Engineering team, part of Amazon's Last Mile organization. The Last Mile team helps get customer packages from delivery stations to a customer's doorstep.

This is a unique opportunity to own high-impact engineering programs and mechanisms that advance the intelligence and reliability of our last mile business. We are looking for an individual who has experience creating scalable, data-driven solutions to complex reliability and engineering problems. In this role, you will be responsible for driving engineering program governance, compliance reporting, data analytics, and documentation systems that enable leadership visibility, cross-functional alignment, and operational excellence across a portfolio of automation and electrical infrastructure projects.

You will build and maintain the mechanisms that keep our engineering organization running at the highest standard—from automated dashboards and compliance reporting to documentation platforms and stakeholder coordination. You will partner with field engineers, electrical contractors, supply chain teams, and operations leaders to deliver scalable processes that reduce rework, improve quality, and accelerate project delivery.

Key competencies of this position include insisting on the highest standards in root cause quality and corrective action effectiveness; analyzing and deep diving systems performance; inventing and simplifying solutions that improve installation and operational processes; and providing technical expertise to internal customers and stakeholders.

Key job responsibilities

Design and maintain automated reporting pipelines and performance dashboards (e.g., equipment health trends, failure rates, system uptime) that provide leadership with real-time visibility into program health and enable data-driven decisions
Translate complex data sets into clear narratives and actionable recommendations for stakeholders at all levels, supporting weekly business reviews and program prioritization
Build and maintain AI-powered compliance tools that aggregate multi-source data (invoices, training records, action items) into consolidated weekly leadership reports
Manage multiple concurrent engineering projects (electrical, automation, MHE) across the NA delivery station network, coordinating timelines and deliverables with external contractors
Track project milestones and completion metrics; identify process gaps through root cause analysis and implement corrective actions that reduce rework and accelerate project delivery
Own weekly organizational compliance reporting on a strict cadence; monitor metrics including training completion, invoice accuracy, and Correction of Error action item closure
Administer engineering documentation platforms and develop SOPs that standardize processes across the network; drive document governance including version control, review cycles, and user enablement
Collaborate cross-functionally with Supply Chain, Startup Execution, Operations, RME, and external contractors; facilitate status meetings and manage escalations from field engineers through senior leadership

A day in the life

No two days look alike in this role. You will move fluidly between analyzing performance data and building dashboards, facilitating cross-functional alignment meetings, and designing scalable process improvements that eliminate rework across the network. You balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution—architecting a new reporting mechanism one hour and removing barriers for field teams the next. You thrive in ambiguity, take ownership of problems before they are assigned, and find energy in the variety of challenges that come with supporting and driving measurable impact across a fast-moving engineering organization operating at Amazon scale.

About The Team

Our diverse team of engineers and program managers owns the full lifecycle, from firm engineering through project execution to final customer hand-off. We are customer-obsessed, data-driven, and never satisfied with the status quo. We capture lessons learned, incorporate them into our mechanisms, and raise the quality bar with each iteration. Our approach to growth is holistic—we continually learn, develop, and expand expertise across the organization, leveraging subject matter knowledge on a global scale. Collaboration is at our core; we are a true team that supports, challenges, and leverages each other's strengths to deliver on the Customer Promise every day.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, management, or technology
Experience leading cross-functional teams across engineering, operations, and field execution through launch readiness and go-live phases
Knowledge of AutoCAD, VBA, and SQL at the intermediate level
3+ years of maintenance or engineering experience
Experience managing multiple projects and priorities across teams in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
Experience in written and verbal communication with the ability to present complex technical information in a clear and concise manner to executives and non-technical leaders

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building launch readiness frameworks, standard work, playbooks, and scalable deployment mechanisms across multiple concurrent sites
Master's degree in engineering, management, or technology
Experience in creating process improvements with automation and analysis, or experience working with large-scale data mining and reporting tools (i.e. SQL, MS Power Query, Python)
Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings, or experience developing MOPs and SWMS for planned works
Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification

Description

Application deadline: Aug 29, 2026

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services is looking for a Infrastructure Technical Program Manager to support and deploy one of the world’s largest and most complex telecommunication networks. The role is responsible for the execution of a strategic plan to improve the business processes and deployment of hyper-scaled cloud infrastructure, creation of a quality control system for North and South America (NASA), pre/post-inspections for design validation, and piloting stakeholder communication for delivery schedules. This opportunity is within the Global Connectivity Infrastructure Delivery - Fiber Deployment organization, which is responsible for project management, quality and delivery of fiber capacity for the physical network solutions that drive Amazon’s internal infrastructure and connect our services to the world.

Key job responsibilities

Reporting and Leadership: Reports to NASA GCID-FD Deployment Manager; provides regular updates to NASA and Global Senior management
Strategic Partnership: Serves as key member of North/South America GCID-FD team, driving overall Network Infrastructure strategy
Vendor Management: Manages vendor delivery timelines, measures progress, and rates performance through quality KPIs
Quality Program Development: Builds quality management program tracking defects, mitigating risks, standardizing root cause analysis, and implementing performance measures
Reporting and Stakeholder Communication: Creates standardized reporting for MFP&A; delivers regular deployment progress updates to management and stakeholders
Network Plan Tracking: Manages approved network plans with internal customers and construction vendors through to in-service delivery
Cross-Functional Program Management: Simultaneously manages multiple competing projects/programs, some at global scale
Daily Collaboration: Interfaces with engineers, technicians, vendors, and senior management
Physical Audits: Audits completed construction, reviews fiber test results, and hands off deliverables to internal customers
Risk and Escalation Management: Anticipates bottlenecks, manages risk/escalations, and balances business needs vs. technical constraints
Site Access Coordination: Coordinates access and approvals for security-regulated sites

A day in the life

This role oversees deployment of infrastructure, and iterative procedural changes. This includes travel to the field, generation of weekly reports, and updating standards and specifications for a global deployment team. This position requires onsite visits to physical locations and is not a full time remote job. Physical inspections and learning the technical standards for outside and inside fiber plant is required.

About The Team

The Global Connectivity Infrastructure Delivery - Fiber Deployment (GCID-FD) team is responsible for planning, managing, and delivering physical fiber optic network infrastructure across North and South America. The team partners with construction vendors, engineers, and internal stakeholders to deploy large-scale fiber networks on time and to the highest quality standards. Through rigorous vendor management, quality control programs, and cross-functional collaboration, GCID-FD ensures network infrastructure moves from approved plans to in-service delivery. The team drives network strategy, manages risk, and coordinates complex deployments across security-regulated sites to support global connectivity goals.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of technical infrastructure management experience
Knowledge of best practices and emerging technologies, related to infrastructure (i.e. network, data center, hardware, software)
Experience with varying scenarios of infrastructure builds
You must have 3+ years experience managing third-party construction or infrastructure vendors, including tracking delivery timelines, measuring performance through KPIs, and implementing corrective actions when quality standards.
You must have 3+ years experience auditing completed construction, reviewing fiber test results or similar deliverables, and coordinating site access in security-regulated environments.
You must have 3+ years experience proactively identifying deployment bottlenecks, managing escalations, and balancing business needs against technical constraints to keep projects on track.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a network planning, network construction/implementation, or commercial implementation role at an ISP, telecoms operator, or Hyperscaler

Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago provides superior pediatric care in a setting that offers the latest benefits and innovations in medical technology, research and family-friendly design. As the largest pediatric provider in the region with a 140-year legacy of excellence, kids and their families are at the center of all we do. Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago is ranked in all 10 specialties by the U.S. News & World Report.

Location

680 Lake Shore Drive

Job Description

The Program Coordinator of Food, Activity and Nutrition (FAN) Initiatives builds community and clinical partnerships by leading capacity and awareness building activities to support the coordination, communication and evaluation of food, activity and nutrition programs and initiatives within the Patrick M. Magoon Institute for Healthy Communities. This includes coordinating the implementation of existing FAN programs and assisting with the planning, development, and implementation of future initiatives. This position directly supports food access programming for patients and works collaboratively with external community partners and internal Lurie programs.

The position helps advance Lurie Children’s broader mission to improve the health and wellbeing of children, youth, families and communities by supporting community health initiatives, site operations and special projects aligned with the priorities of the Patrick M. Magoon Institute for Healthy Communities and the Community Health Improvement Strategy.

This position is part of the Food, Activity and Nutrition Initiatives team within the Patrick M. Magoon Institute for Healthy Communities, Lurie Children’s hub for community-focused initiatives. The Magoon Institute brings together clinical care, advocacy, research, education and community engagement to advance community health and health equity for infants, children, adolescents and families across Chicago. The Institute also leads Lurie Children’s Community Health Needs Assessment and Community Health Improvement Strategy, which guide the hospital’s community health priorities and investments.

The Food, Activity and Nutrition (FAN) Initiatives team collaborates with key partners on local, state-wide and national levels to help ensure that supports for healthy eating and being physically active are always within reach for youth and their families where they live, learn, and play. FAN aims to improve the health and well-being of Chicagoland children, adolescents, and their families by addressing nutrition security, physical activity, and related chronic health conditions through community partnership, clinical collaboration, and improving upstream health factors.

This is a hybrid position. Team members are expected to work from the office (680 N. Lake Shore Dr., Chicago, IL) at least one day per week. Some weeks may require additional days in the office.

Application Requirements

All applicants must submit a resume and cover letter. Resumes should be no more than 2 pages. Cover letters should describe the candidate's interest in the position and their areas of interest within food, nutrition, and physical activity space. Cover letters should be no more than 1 page.

Job Functions

Coordinate community-clinic efforts related to nutrition and physical activity. Strengthen connections between Lurie Children's healthcare providers and FAN community partners by coordinating processes that facilitate referrals, resource recommendations and care extension models to ensure that children and their families can access and make use of FAN related resources after discharge. 
Serve as community-level liaison and point-of-contact on food, activity and nutrition-related topics, programs and policies; represents FAN and Lurie Children’s at community and city food, activity and nutrition meetings, coalitions and collaborations.
Coordinate and assist with planning, developing, implementing and evaluating food, activity and nutrition initiatives within the Magoon Institute, in collaboration with FAN team and internal and external partners. Support project alignment with community priorities, FAN strategies, Magoon Institute community health strategy and Lurie Children’s mission.
Build and maintain relationships with community-based organizations and other local institutions such as food pantries, schools, parks, places of worship, local businesses and community coalitions via awareness and capacity building activities, including 1-on-1 meetings and working groups. Support community, region and city-wide convenings, coordinate trainings and workshops and assist with action planning and strategy development and implementation.
Facilitate collection, tracking and reporting of data and other project activities in a timely manner to demonstrate impact for internal reporting, grant applications, stewardship reports and other related requests.
Support development of written output, including new grant proposals, program reporting, and marketing materials.
Develop and disseminate patient educational messaging, toolkits, handouts and other health promotion and educational resources that support FAN strategies to ensure accessibility and increase community level capacity and awareness.
Assist with the development, implementation and expansion of a coordinated approach to community engagement and facilitate sharing of identified models with the Magoon Institute team.
Support opportunities to engage Lurie Children’s leaders, employees, physicians and trainees in community health efforts and neighborhood activities.
Other job functions as assigned.

Associate degree required, bachelor’s degree in public health or related field preferred. An equivalent combination of education and/or experience may be considered in lieu of the degree when the experience has been directly related to the duties of the job.

Greenwood Rising is a community-centered space dedicated to preserving and sharing the history and resilience of Tulsa’s Historic Greenwood District, once known as Black Wall Street. The Program Coordinator will also work directly with the Assistant Director to ensure that Center programs and events align with leadership initiatives and the Work-Learning-Service (WLS) student team to embed targeted learning outcomes into the student work experience, preparing students to make positive contributions to the campus community and beyond.

Following long-standing tradition and practice at Berea College, this position includes responsibility for supervising, mentoring, and developing students in the College's integrated Work College Program. This supports student learning, career readiness, and the program's learning goals and outcomes. The Work College Program provides a developmental framework that guides student learning while creating a structured mentorship opportunity, with role-specific training that equips faculty and staff mentors to support student development. Faculty and staff mentors play an essential part in helping students connect their work-learning-service experiences with broader academic, professional, and personal development. For faculty, this aligns with Berea's tenure and promotion criteria.

Your Key Responsibilities

Program Coordination & Event Management – 30%

Plan, implement, facilitate, execute, and evaluate programs and events to ensure Black students have appropriate access to new knowledge, supportive resources, community building, and other targeted outcomes.
Ensure that programs are communicated internally and externally through appropriate marketing channels, providing equitable engagement for all Black Cultural Center programs, initiatives, and events.
Embed learning outcomes directly into the WLS student work experience, creating opportunities for Black students to gain hands-on experience with event coordination and planning.
Create a programming calendar each academic year, ensuring equitable access for students to engage with BCC programs and initiatives.
Plan and facilitate a monthly Kula Kusoma event, providing students with the opportunity to engage with Berea alumni through meaningful dialogue and relevant topics of discussion.

Advising, Teaching, and Lesson Planning – 20%

Teach a minimum of two courses per Academic Year (Fall/Spring), including but not limited to AFR 100: Models & Mentors for Success, in collaboration with the African and African American Studies department.
Serve as an Academic Advisor to a student caseload in collaboration with The NEST (Navigating Engagement, Success, and Transition): Student Success Central.

Student Engagement & Support – 20%

Facilitate “The Collective,” a monthly discussion group for Black students, creating intentional spaces for students to bridge gaps amongst the diaspora, providing opportunities for students to engage in conversations while maintaining a safe, productive learning environment.
Engage and collaborate with the African Student Association (ASA), Black Student Union (BSU), and other Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs) through programmatic efforts and intentional collaboration.
Serve and support students participating in BME, including Black students, Latinx students, Appalachian and Non-Appalachian White students, LGBTQIA+ students, and others who find community through the ensemble.
Assist the Director and Assistant Director with leading onboarding and training sessions for BCC student leaders, including WLS student team members, Registered Student Organizations, and others, as assigned.

Administrative Operations – 10%

Assist the Director in managing the Center budget, spaces, and resources, particularly as it pertains to the programming budget allocated to educational experiences, cultural competencies, and initiative specific priorities.

Marketing & Outreach – 10%

Serve on campus-wide committees, as assigned, to broaden the involvement and advocacy for the Black Cultural Center and the Black student experience.

Assessment & Reporting – 5%

Assess effectiveness of assigned programs and services through comprehensive data reporting to track engagement, retention, and academic outcomes

Departmental and Divisional Projects – 5%

Complete all duties as assigned by the Director, Assistant Director, Associate Vice President or Vice President

What You'll Bring

Education required to ensure success in this position:

A master's degree in Black/African American Studies, History, Culture, or a related field with an emphasis on people, culture, and community engagement.

Experience required to ensure success in this position:

2-3 years of primary leadership experience in an education setting, preferably higher education, working directly with students in a multicultural or diversity affairs-related position.
Direct experience in program coordination and student support, especially for students of color

Special Skills, knowledge and abilities:

Exemplary oral and written communication skills.
Strong administrative and organizational skills.
Ability to facilitate, delegate, and create a vision and processes to be implemented with targeted outcomes
Thorough familiarity with theory, research, and practice in student engagement and success, and in multicultural understanding, especially as focused on race and interracial understanding.
Ability to design and implement meaningful and high-quality co-curricular programs for students.
Deep personal commitment to multicultural understanding.

License, certification, or registration necessary:

Valid driver's license preferred.
Required background checks

Physical Requirements:

Ability to navigate campus/public buildings and grounds
Ability to travel independently by car and/or plane
Ability to occasionally lift up to 20 lbs.

Environmental conditions:

Professional office environment with interruptions and noise due to frequent visitors, students, staff and faculty
Occasional travel is required for meetings, conferences, etc.

Standard office equipment: computer, fax, phone, etc.
Media equipment
College-operated cars, minivans, or 12/15-passenger vans

Founded in 1855, Berea College is nationally recognized as the first coeducational and interracial college in the South. Berea has a longstanding commitment to interracial education and is one of the most racially diverse private liberal arts colleges in the United States. With an emphasis on service to Appalachia and beyond, Berea enrolls more than 1,500 students from 44 states and U.S. territories and more than 60 countries. Berea College admits students who are unable to afford tuition and provides every enrolled student with a fully funded degree that covers 100% of tuition, housing, food, supplies, and fees without loans, for all four years. Berea’s students excel in the College’s supportive yet demanding academic environment, and most are the first in their families to attend college. As one of only 10 federally recognized Work Colleges, all Berea students work 10-12 hours weekly in various positions across campus, building professional skills in a real-world learning environment. Washington Monthly ranked Berea College the #1 Best College for your Tuition and Tax Dollars, 2025. Berea also ranks #1 in educational access by The New York Times , 2023 and #1 for lowest educational debt by U.S. News and World Report , 2025 and 2026. Berea College is also the only institution in Kentucky to receive the 5-Star Rating from Money Magazine, 2026.

Located where the Bluegrass Region meets the Cumberland Mountains, the town of Berea (pop. 17,000) lies 40 miles south of Lexington and is approximately two hours from Cincinnati, Louisville, and Knoxville. More information about Berea College is available at www.berea.edu.

Berea College, in light of its mission in the tradition of impartial love and social equality, welcomes all people of the earth to learn and work here.

Our Benefits

Berea College offers a comprehensive benefits package to eligible employees and their families including health care, dental, vision, retirement, health savings accounts, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability and an Employee Assistance Program. The benefit package also includes access to the Child Development Laboratory for children of College Staff, ages 6 weeks to 6 years, Seabury Center Membership, Staff Development Funds and Tuition Reimbursement.

Eligible staff employees also receive paid holidays, vacation, and sick leave.

Part-time employees who work an average of twenty-four hours per week over the course of a year, receive benefits on a pro-rated basis.

To learn more details, visit our benefits page at https://www.berea.edu/human-resources/employee-benefits.

Our Unique Culture

Berea College strives to be a place where people with various Christian interpretations, different religious traditions, and no religious traditions work together in support of Berea's Great Commitments.

Over the past century, various leaders of the College have applied the College’s inclusive scriptural foundation and spirit to their expanding world and welcomed those whose beliefs were consistent with the Christian gospel of impartial love. Therefore, Berea College today affirms its inclusive Christian tradition even as it respects the traditions of Jews, Muslims, Buddhists, and Hindus, as well as other faiths, and those holding no religious beliefs. We strive not to ignore our differences, but rather seek to understand each other honestly and respectfully, and together create a climate where anyone can openly discuss what they believe without fear of sanction. To that end, all persons who are willing to share in the spirit and the work of the Great Commitments as shaped by its preamble are welcome to study, to teach, and to work at Berea

Labor Supervision

In support of Berea College’s great commitments, staff and faculty serve as labor supervisors. Our fourth great commitment, The Dignity of Labor, promotes learning and serving in community through the student Labor Program, honoring the dignity and utility of all work, mental and manual, and taking pride in work well done. Student Labor Supervision includes scheduling, assigning, and approving student work, developing students' workplace acumen, and providing tangible work experience. A wonderful opportunity for an experienced mental health professional to assume a leadership role on

Grounded in the Catholic vision of the human person, Joseph House is a residential re-entry community in Tallahassee, FL. We create communities of welcome where men returning from incarceration encounter the healing of home, authentic relationships, and clinical excellence in trauma-informed care. We operate on a non-discriminatory, nonsectarian basis and welcome staff of all backgrounds and beliefs who share our commitment to human dignity, equality, and second chances.

Position Overview
Role:
Social Worker (Full-Time Exempt)
Location:
On-site — Tallahassee, Florida (with local community navigation)
Compensation:
$50,000 – $60,000/year + Generous PTO & Diocesan Benefits (Medical, Dental, Vision, HSA with employer contributions, employer-paid Long-Term Disability & Life Insurance, and 401(k) retirement plan).
Hours:
Flexible 40-hour week. Primary hours incorporate afternoons/early evenings (e.g., 10:00 AM – 6:30 PM, M–F) to align with resident employment and vocational schedules.
Reports To:
Clinical Director

The Opportunity
We are seeking a compassionate social worker to provide dedicated case management and re-entry navigation for our intimate residential community of 6 to 8 male residents
re-entering society from state/federal prison (including individuals with non-violent, violent, and sexual offenses).

Working with a low resident-to-staff ratio, you will serve as the primary bridge between clinical therapeutic care and daily real-world reintegration. You will work within a collaborative team alongside the Clinical Director, a full-time Health and Wellness Manager, and a full-time House Manager.

In our tiered crisis framework, the Social Worker provides primary case management and daytime crisis support alongside on-site residential staff. During off-business hours, initial on-site operations and de-escalation are managed by residential house staff. The Social Worker serves as a Tier-3 contact for off-hours in case of emergencies only. The Tier-2 coordination is provided by the Clinical Director (coordinating crisis referrals, community resources, or care team communications).

Key Responsibilities

Supportive Case Management:

Qualifications

Experience:

Deep commitment to working with justice-involved individuals with objectivity, clear professional boundaries, and compassion.
Requirements:

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis (priority deadline: August 28, 2026

.

In this role, you'll help shape the future of tissue and hygiene for billions of people worldwide.

In this role you will lead and deliver a comprehensive, on-site Occupational Health (OH) service, encompassing (but not limited to) health surveillance and biological monitoring, drug and alcohol screening, fitness-for-work assessments, case management, and health promotion. You perform at the highest level possible, and you appreciate a performance culture fuelled by authentic caring. You want to be part of a company actively dedicated to sustainability, inclusion, wellbeing, and career development.

We’ll be Unstoppable Together.

To work with the Mill EHS Team to help identify potential health hazards, participate in the assessment and control of risk, and manage fitness for task and health surveillance programmes in line with local and global standards, and OH CoE clinical standard operating procedures.
To provide specialist OH advice, within the scope of the role, on the potential health impacts arising from physical, chemical, biological, and psychosocial hazards.

Our integrated services include primary care, women’s health, pediatrics, behavioral health, dental, optometry, dermatology, pharmacy, laboratory services, and care coordination.

As a Medical Care Coordinator, you will work collaboratively with the Program Manager and interdisciplinary care team to implement individualized clinical care plans and address the social and practical barriers that can prevent patients from receiving quality care.   You’ll build meaningful relationships with patients, help them understand and achieve their health goals, coordinate appointments and follow-up care, and communicate progress to providers and care managers. Your work will directly contribute to improved patient experiences, stronger continuity of care, and better health outcomes.

Coordinate Patient Care

Conduct health risk assessments and help develop strategies to address identified social determinants of health and care barriers.
Coordinate medical and specialty appointments for patients referred by providers, Care Managers, and other members of the care team.
Provide appointment reminders and post-visit follow-up calls.
Support patients in understanding and following their individualized care management plans and self-care goals.
Coordinate continuity of care between Eisner Health and external healthcare organizations, facilities, and providers.
Follow up promptly with patients after hospitalizations and emergency room visits, including obtaining discharge summaries and relevant medical records.
Conduct home or facility visits, when necessary, to support adherence to the plan of care.

Build Patient Relationships

Serve as a trusted liaison between patients, families, providers, Care Managers, and clinic staff.
Provide culturally responsive information, education, and support through phone calls and other patient interactions.
Help patients establish, maintain, and achieve clinically based self-management goals.
Provide disease-specific and preventive care education.
Support Eisner Health’s trauma-informed care approach in every patient interaction.

Collaborate Across the Care Team

Participate in patient-centered team meetings focused on improving patient outcomes and operational processes.
Participate in clinical cross-care-team meetings.
Provide timely updates to Primary Care Providers and Care Managers regarding patient progress, barriers, and self-management.
Serve as a liaison between frontline clinic staff, clinicians, and other appropriate team members.
Support population health management activities as assigned.
Assist with the maintenance and dissemination of the chronic care model across appropriate clinic staff.

Document & Improve

Maintain patient confidentiality in accordance with organizational policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
Identify and pursue more efficient ways to deliver excellent patient and staff experiences.

Associate or Bachelor’s degree in health or social services or
at least a year of experience in a clinical setting.
Bilingual English/Spanish required.

Strong organizational, verbal, and written communication skills.
Ability to facilitate and coordinate patient care plans.

Experience working with an Electronic Health Record (EHR) and entering patient data.
Experience in care coordination, care management, community health, or a similar healthcare environment.

new_jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION---HOUSING SUPPORTS CASE MANAGER

Overview: Family
Promise of Essex County seeks a motivated, compassionate, and organized social services professional to fill the role of Housing Supports Case Manager (HSCM). The HSCM is responsible for conducting outreach to individuals who are referred to FPE for housing support services and providing supportive case management to eligible households. Utilizing a housing first approach, HSCM will assist eligible households with all aspects related to securing and maintaining permanent housing. The HSCM will report to the Manager of Family Programs. This is a non-exempt position.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

1. Outreach and Housing Navigation

·        Conduct ongoing community outreach, engaging with referred individuals requiring housing support services. Outreach may include engaging with individuals and families experiencing unsheltered homelessness in their communities (i.e., encampment communities, under bridges, and emergency shelters, etc.)
·        Field telephone and walk-in inquiries regarding housing support services
·        Conduct needs assessments to determine individualized goals to overcome barriers for people experiencing homelessness
·        Provide housing navigation services, assisting with transportation and system navigation skills to access documentation necessary to qualify individuals and families for housing. Navigation may include transporting clients and walking alongside them to obtain necessary documentation including birth certificates, identification documents, income verifications, etc.
·        Provide support and guidance throughout the document acquisition process, including assistance with completing forms and making necessary appointments.
-         Offer translations services or other accommodations for individuals who have limited English proficiency or other disabilities.
·        Provide linkages to services for financial assistance to help individuals pay for necessary fees, such as those associated with obtaining documentation or related to renting an apartment
·        Assist with the housing search and leasing process by accompanying enrolled households to view units
·        Act as a liaison between clients and landlords or property managers, advocating for client needs, during the process of locating and leasing safe, secure housing
·        Other duties as assigned
2. Supportive Case Management

·        Provide direct case management services to enrolled households on a weekly basis for up to 12 months, appropriate to their prioritized needs
·        Collaboratively with households, identify goals and supportive services needed to maintain permanent housing, economic stability, and overall wellness
·         Develop individualized, goal-oriented service plans to enhance stability, safety and self-sufficiency for the household and its individual members.
·        Assist enrolled households with locating and securing community and housing resources (i.e., utility assistance, furniture assistance, food support, etc.)
·        Coordinate clients’ services, including medical, employment, education, and counseling, with other agencies as needed
·        Support enrolled households as they navigate shifting into permanent housing, understanding that households may need support in following their lease requirements and managing tasks like paying rent and bills on time, managing relationships with neighbors or property managers, etc.
·        Participate in case conference with other social services team members to collaborate around ways to best support enrolled households
·        Other duties as assigned

3.      Coordination with DCA, Field Offices, and Medicaid MCOs

·        Assist households referred by DCA and/or OHP, Medicaid MCOs, or other referring entities
·        Collaborate with Medicaid MCO staff assigned to clients for status updates.
·        Ongoing case collaboration with DCA, OHP, Medicaid MCOs as needed
·        Other coordination as assigned

4.       General

·        Comply with the FPE Employee Handbook, including confidentiality standards.
·        Ensure that case management notes and services are delivered in keeping with NASW Standards for Case Management and its Code of Ethics.
·        Cultivate and develop relationships and partnerships that will assist families including networking with landlords and employer partners.
·        Ensure that all required documentation is maintained in accordance with accepted standards and in compliance with government and foundation grants. This includes regularly updating case notes/files and statistical information necessary for reporting levels of service and outcomes.
·        Maintain service records in the federal Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) and Electronic Health Record, entering contacts within 24 hours of service delivery
·        Attend and contribute to specific weekly updates to staff meetings.
·        Attend appropriate government and community meetings.
·        Other duties as assigned
Education, Experience and Skills

The successful candidate is enthusiastic and can display good judgment, take initiative, communicate clearly and professionally, demonstrate respect and collaboration, and work independently as well as with a team.
Minimum Education Requirements: Bachelor Degree in Human Services preferred or a minimum of two year degree in Human related services and two years related experience. 
Excellent communication skills, particularly listening, mediation and writing skills.
Possess strong organizational skills with ability to meet demanding workload.
Creative thinker/adaptive personality.
Knowledge or understanding of tenant’s rigs and responsibilities as well as “strengths based” case management.
Concentrated record keeping, budgeting, and mathematical skills; ability to produce required reports to federal, state, and local government agencies and funding sources.
Demonstrated knowledge of community resources, social service agencies and landlords.
Fluency in English language is required. Spanish speaking ability is an added asset, but not required.
Valid driver’s license and car.
Sensitivity to cultural and socioeconomic characteristics of population served.
The ability to work collaboratively with other personnel and/or service providers or professionals.
The capacity to maintain a role to empower clients and to intervene appropriately to meet service goals.
Knowledge and comfort with basic computer programs, including Microsoft Office.
Experience with Medicaid MCOs and Electronic Health Records is a plus

Salary $53,000

Benefits Include:

Paid Time Off
Health, dental, vision, life benefits
Education benefits
401k Plans

No phone calls please.

What You’ll Do

Provide day-to-day leadership, direction and support to a team of Fire Prevention Inspectors, ensuring inspections, reporting and follow-up activities are completed consistently and in accordance with legislative requirements;
Coordinate and oversee the Fire Prevention Inspection Program, including inspection scheduling, workload planning, quality assurance and program performance;

Prepare procurement documents, oversee service contracts and monitor vendor performance to ensure quality service delivery;
Lead public education and fire prevention initiatives by coordinating awareness campaigns, reviewing educational materials and supporting consistent messaging for staff and tenants;
Prepare reports and maintain records detailing information about property, infractions observed and actions to be taken;
Establish client communication protocols, financial reporting mechanisms, progress updates, scheduling and work activities to meet/exceed contract obligations;
Supervise, mentor, train and direct unionized service and administrative staff;
Manage staff’s attendance including vacation requests, payroll input and monitoring of staffing capacity (shifts, on call, call-out schedules, etc.);

Other projects/initiatives and duties as required.

Post-Secondary education in Fire Protection Technology, or an equivalent of combination of directly relevant education and experience;
Minimum of 3-5 years of job-related experience including technical and legislative knowledge and experience in contract administration, tender preparation, and development and monitoring of budget plans;
Demonstrated knowledge of the Ontario Fire Code, Ontario Building Code, Occupational Health and Safety Act, Residential Tenancies Act and other related legislation, by-laws and applicable standards;
Excellent interpersonal/ public relations/teamwork skills;
Experience in the preparation of reports, correspondence and record maintenance;
Possesses strong negotiating skills and the ability to analyze and evaluate complex problems provide solutions and recommend alternatives;
Possesses advanced skills in computer applications such use of Microsoft Word, Project and Excel;
Excellent communication skills both oral and written;
Excellent customer service skills and experience in providing respectful service;
Previous experience in dealing with the public in enforcement situations or experience in construction, architecture or engineering is an asset.
Experience supervising unionized staff would be considered an asset;

What's Next

Once you apply, we’ll review your resume to determine if your skills and experience match the qualifications for the role and only qualified candidates will be contacted for next steps. If you move forward, the process may include an interview, written/practical test, and reference check.

This is an 18-month fixed-term contract and can be a fully remote role, giving you the flexibility to work from anywhere in the UK, with optional office access if desired. As an alternative location, we will also consider candidates based in the US Eastern Time Zone.

The Role

Partner with workstream delivery teams and project managers to turn transformation objectives into practical delivery plans, milestones and execution roadmaps.
Build and maintain integrated program plans, milestone trackers, RAID logs, risk registers and status dashboards to provide clear visibility of progress.
Drive day-to-day program execution, ensuring activities remain aligned to agreed objectives, timelines and outcomes.
Identify and manage dependencies, constraints, risks and critical path activities, escalating issues with clear recommendations and mitigation options.
Coordinate across delivery teams to ensure key deliverables are completed on schedule and to agreed quality standards.
Provide structured updates to program leadership and stakeholders on progress, risks, issues, dependencies and decisions.
Establish and manage governance cadences, including steering committee reviews, workstream check-ins and escalation protocols.
Build strong working relationships with HRLT, HRIT, Internal Comms and Change Management, Legal, Finance, AI TMO and functional leaders.
Ensure HRIT and change management deliverables are integrated into program planning, readiness, training and communications activity.
Promote best practice program management standards and capture lessons learned to improve future transformation initiatives.
Ensure the program is aligned to and tracking against the financial goals and targets (investment, savings).

Qualifications

What you’ll bring

Significant project or program management experience delivering complex global transformation in a large enterprise environment.
Experience in HR transformation, operating model transformation, technology-enabled change or large-scale business change programs.
A track record of managing multiple cross-functional projects or workstreams simultaneously, including dependencies, risks and stakeholder expectations.
Experience supporting executive governance forums and preparing clear, decision-focused leadership reporting materials.
Strong stakeholder management, facilitation and meeting management skills, with the confidence to drive alignment and decisions in ambiguous environments.
Structured and disciplined delivery skills, with the ability to translate strategic objectives into practical plans and measurable outcomes.
Working knowledge of both waterfall and agile or hybrid delivery methodologies.
An analytical mindset, with confidence using data, metrics and technology to inform decisions and status reporting.
Practical experience using generative AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT or equivalent, to improve productivity, problem-solving and business outcomes.
A bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; project management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2, Agile or MSP is desirable.

What We Offer

Enjoy a benefits package designed to help you thrive, both professionally and personally. You'll receive 25 days of annual leave plus an extra WTW day to relax and recharge. Our comprehensive health and wellbeing offering includes private healthcare, life insurance, group income protection, and regular health assessments, all giving you peace of mind. Secure your future with our defined contribution pension scheme, featuring matched contributions up to 10% from the company.

We support your growth and balance with hybrid working options, access to an employee assistance programme, and a fully paid volunteer day to make a difference in your community. On top of these, you can opt into a variety of additional perks including an electric vehicle car scheme, share scheme, cycle-to-work programme, dental and optical cover, critical illness protection, and much more. Start making the most of your career and wellbeing with a range of benefits tailored for you.

Equal Opportunity Employer

The Global Real Estate and Facilities (GREF) organization seeks a strategic support partner to transform how we leverage AI-powered insights and translate them into critical execution plans across our EMEA portfolio. AI-Powered Insights & Decision Enablement

You will conduct deep-dive analyses that challenge conventional thinking, translating complex datasets into recommendations that shape portfolio decisions and areas of investment. Your creative problem-solving will introduce innovative methodologies for sizing and prioritizing the most impactful opportunities across listening channels, aligning stakeholders on prioritization and execution of initiatives to improve customer experience and controllership across our matrixed organization.
You will drive insights to action by building compelling narratives that secure leadership commitment.
You will develop nimble, low-friction frameworks that accelerate decision-making and improve decision quality.
You will design and run business reviews that enable leadership to track performance, identify risks, and adjust course. Your ability to synthesize data from service requests, performance metrics, employee feedback, and operational costs will enable predictive insights.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Execution

You will operate comfortably across domains, building partnerships with Business Intelligence, Technology, Operations, Regional Teams, Finance, Customer Insights, and Design and Construction. You will navigate ambiguity and wear many hats—moving fluidly from analytical deep dives to tactical execution. When launching initiatives, you will advise stakeholders on Operational Support teams to engage—Customer Insights for research, Help Desk for service support, Communications for change management.
You will partner with regional teams to implement data-driven improvements and lead transformation programs that reduce service defects.
